blocks.text: Carbon has two oxides, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. Carbon monoxide is produced mainly by the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels, 2C(s) + O2(g) gives 2CO(g). It is a highly poisonous gas that causes suffocation when inhaled: it binds blood haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen does, excluding oxygen from normal respiration; the poisoning can be reversed by giving high-pressure oxygen. Carbon dioxide is the key greenhouse gas emitted by human activities such as the combustion of fossil fuels, C(s) + O2(g) gives CO2(g); it is a primary greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere, leading to global warming.

blocks.prompt: What common human activity raises the level of carbon monoxide in the air, and why is CO dangerous even in small amounts (MCQ V)?
blocks.explanation: Petrol-driven vehicles, whose engines burn fuel incompletely, are the common source. CO is dangerous because haemoglobin binds it far more strongly than oxygen, so even a low concentration ties up the blood's oxygen carriers and suffocates the tissues.

items: CO from incomplete combustion (2C + O2 gives 2CO): binds haemoglobin, poisonous; CO2 from complete combustion: the key greenhouse gas.
